First thing first, practice the following office phrases and use them liberally:

"I can do that, however I currently have the following items on my plate...(list items). I will check with my supervisor on when I can get this completed. What is your ideal timeline? Ok, I will send you a follow up email after speaking to my supervisor."

"I haven't been shown how to do this yet. Can you show me how to do it or direct me to someone who can?"

"I'm fairly confident in using this software, but can you show me how you use it in this context?"

"Can you explain how/where this fits in the workflow, just so I can wrap my brain around it."

"I'm still on a learning curve, can you re-explain that and give me context on what you mean by...(insert whatever you are confused about)"

If people start throwing around jargon or acronyms you don't understand, stop them right then and repeat the acronym and ask them what it stands for.

Also, carry a notebook around with you EVERYWHERE and take notes on everything. Even if it seems like obvious information. I promise, that one obvious instruction you will forget. Also, it makes you look sharp. When I worked temp jobs I always got asked to become perm and in my review they would comment on how I was the only person to take notes and they liked that.

Also, it's never personal. No one cares how you feel or what you are going through. They have a project that needs to get done, then they want to get home to deal with their own problems. Don't get all defensive and freaked out that people are "against you". They aren't. They just need to get shit done. And honestly, you sound really defensive right now. You have to get professional if you want to go anywhere. No one will put up with a drama queen/king in the office. There is too much competition in this job market. And I doubt it will get better at a different place. It sounds more like a your problem instead of a them problem (just being honest).
